core_summary: This chapter develops two-dimensional surface measurement: Perimeter (total boundary length) and Area (enclosed 2D surface region) for rectangles, squares, regular polygons, and composite shapes. It establishes the principle of area conservation under cutting/re-arrangement and analyzes perimeter variation for fixed areas.
key_concepts: Perimeter Formulas: Rectangle P = 2(l + w); Square P = 4s; Regular n-gon P = n x s.
Area Formulas: Rectangle A = l x w; Square A = s^2.
Area Conservation: Cutting and re-arranging a flat shape into different non-overlapping pieces preserves total surface area.
Perimeter Variation: Shapes with identical area can have drastically different perimeters. For a fixed rectangular area, a square minimizes perimeter; elongated strips maximize perimeter.
Composite Area Method: Complex L-shaped or stair-step figures are evaluated by decomposing them into non-overlapping simple rectangles and summing sub-areas.

key_terms.definition: The total linear distance around the outer boundary of a closed planar shape.
The magnitude of two-dimensional surface space enclosed within the boundary of a closed plane figure.
A closed 2D polygon with all sides of equal length and all interior angles of equal measure.
The property stating that the total area of a shape remains unchanged when decomposed and reassembled.

key_takeaways: Perimeter is a 1D length measurement (cm, m); Area is a 2D surface measurement (sq cm, sq m).
Identical areas do not guarantee identical perimeters.
Decomposing composite figures into simple rectangles simplifies complex area calculations.
